title: Spear Hero’s Cover-Up
paragraphs: This time, I’m being extra cautious in everything I do. After all, it’s the last loop. I don’t know what could change the meeting between Father and big sister, so I can’t afford to miss the moment when Father buys her. That’s why I’ve been keeping track of Father after he made some money, making sure not to lose sight of him. This should be fine for now. Today, I spent the morning hunting with the crimson swine and was pretty fed up. The crimson swine is currently at the town, getting a spa treatment. So I have free time to act. Based on previous loops, I know that around two weeks after the false accusation, Father will buy a slave. Specifically, the monster merchant will approach Father as he walks through an alley. After hitting the red balloon hidden in his pocket with his fist, Father will let out a sigh, looking sorrowful.
“*Sigh…*”
In that alley, the monster merchant will be waiting and approach Father.
“You seem to be in trouble.”
“Hm?”
At first, Father ignores him with a glance and turns away.
“You are short-handed.”
Father stops dead in his tracks.
“You can’t beat the monsters.”
At that, Father’s expression turns irritated as he turns around.
“I’m not looking for help.”
“I’m not offering something so inconvenient as that.”

The merchant steps closer to Father. I’ve seen this kind of thing before… In the first world, I walked through the back alleys of Melromarc, holding my nose from the pig smell, looking for Filo-tan and Father.
“Does this interest you?”
“Stay away, you’re disgusting.”
“Hehe, you have the eyes I like. Alright, I’ll tell you!”
At that moment, something taps my shoulder as I’m watching from a distance.
“*Bububububu!*”
At the noise, Father turns around, and… I meet eyes with the worst possible pig.
W-what are you doing here!?

Stay in the pig farm and play in the mud, you pig! Now, let me explain the situation. The concealment skill and magic are faintly visible to party members. Of course, I can set them to some extent, and they can change depending on the magic or skill.

Damn… I held off on disbanding the party because I didn’t want to raise suspicion, and now it’s backfiring. That’s right… Somehow, the crimson swine managed to sniff me out and came from behind to interrupt me at this very moment.
“*Bubububub? Bubububububub, bubub?*”
The crimson swine is wrapping its arm around mine, acting all provocatively. …Even though I’ve considered everything, to be interrupted at such a terrible time like this…
I’m definitely going to kill him later.
“What? Is Motoyasu over there?”
Damn it… the crimson swine is causing interference right now! This is the last chance! I cannot fail!

I’ve never had this kind of interference in any of the previous loops. Why is he suddenly hindering my actions now!? But I can’t stay hidden forever. I have to drop my concealment skill and reveal myself to Father.
“What are you doing, Naofumi? Who is this guy?”

As I prepare to glare at the crimson swine, feeling murderous, I focus on Father. Here, it’s crucial that the monster merchant doesn’t seem like one of my associates. I absolutely must get Father to buy big sister.
I still think this is within my control!
…Hmph! With a shove, Father pushes the monster merchant aside and stomps off.
“Boo!”
The crimson swine is clearly provoking Father.
“Sigh…”
The monster merchant raises his shoulders lightly in disappointment and walks away.
…Now, how should I deal with this crimson swine?
“Bubububu?”
Your existence is nothing more than a trial for me to meet Filo-tan.
As long as the conditions for meeting Filo-tan are met, I’ll definitely end your life… But to think you’d interfere in the final world… Is killing you the only option?
Damn… If I do something unnecessary, things could get worse. I’ll have to suppress my killing intent and smile at the crimson swine.
“Yeah, that’s right. Now, I have things to do, so I’d like you to let Myne and the others do as they please.”
“Bubub? Bub!”
The crimson swine tilts its head slightly but doesn’t cause any further problems, walking with me part of the way before we separate. After parting with the crimson swine, I start thinking again.
This is bad, very bad! This is the final loop!
What will happen if big sister finds out that Father hasn’t bought a slave? She’ll probably give up on me for sure, and I might never meet Filo-tan again.
I can’t let that happen!

How can I avoid that future? First, is there a way to get Father to buy big sister within the next few days? …It’s not impossible, but big sister will likely be sold elsewhere soon. Even if the monster merchant contacts me again, it’s highly likely that he won’t buy a slave after knowing I’ve met with him.
Hmm? Maybe I can ask for big sister to be sold cheaply? If I do that, could I get the same result as in previous worlds?

Now, I need to focus on the plan! …Even if Father buys big sister, there will likely be problems. That damn crimson swine… causing trouble at this point. I’ll definitely kill him, but now I’m starting to want to do it as brutally as possible. For my life to be ruined because of you after coming this far… It’ll never be enough to just kill you. In summary, I know that big sister usually arrives on the night when the wave occurs.
…Wait. Something’s not right.

Now that I think about it, what did big sister say? I think she mentioned that if she wasn’t in a near-death state, it would take her time to arrive. And last time, she arrived quickly because she died from Father’s angry flames. So if big sister doesn’t end up in a near-death state, it will buy us more time.

No… More importantly, what if I give up on this loop and instead deal with Ren and Itsuki to make the loop happen? The problem is the possibility of big sister entering the loop when it happens. …It’s not an impossible scenario.

What kind of face will big sister make if I trigger the loop without a reason? Even if I make an excuse, she’ll probably get angry. Well, maybe I could just say I bought a different slave, not big sister. But this is the final loop. In that case, this is the last resort: it’s best to keep big sister alive and buy time. Either way, I could have Father hold Sakura-chan’s egg and try to turn her into Filo-tan later, it wouldn’t be too late. Keep big sister alive, confirm Filo-tan’s identity, and then deal with Ren and Itsuki to trigger the loop. If I do it right, I might be able to fool big sister for one full cycle. Since I’ve already lost the last chance, I have no choice but to try this.
“First… I’ll secure big sister.”
I head toward the monster merchant’s tent, put on a mask, and use magic to disguise the voice that caused the failure last time, then purchase big sister.
“Cough!”

Big sister looks frightened, but I can’t offer her any mental care. If the crimson swine finds out I’ve made big sister my ally, I have no idea what he’d do. So, I take big sister to the Shiltvelt area, put her to sleep, and bring her to a inn with a seemingly caring innkeeper, paying them to look after her.

“That was a very scary experience, and I ended up crying loudly. However, I would like you to take care of her for a while. I will pay you… enough money. She’s from the demi-human protection area in Melromarc that was affected by the waves. As for the language… I’ll manage.”
“Y-yes…”

The innkeeper looked at me with confusion, but after seeing the money I provided and observing the older sister’s condition, he nodded as if understanding the gravity of the situation. Demi-humans tend to have a strong sense of solidarity.
“Ah, if you only take the money and leave this child to wander the streets—”

I lightly pointed the spear at the innkeeper and unleashed an intense murderous intent. It seemed that the innkeeper realized he couldn’t refuse my pressure, as he turned pale and nodded repeatedly. I had no room for leniency right now.
“I will come by every day. Farewell.”

With that, I left the older sister at the inn in Shiltvelt, prescribed some medicine, and headed back toward Melromarc. When I searched, I found Father sighing in the Melromarc plains by the riverbank. I used my concealment skill to hide and observed him. I had requested the monster merchant to make contact again. He would try to reach Father within a few days, and I had asked him to speak to me properly during that time. The monster merchant seemed to have grasped Father’s personality from just a brief discussion. It seems the reconnection would take two or three days.
“Oh? There’s a lot today.”
It looked like Father had been punching a balloon, as there was a deflated one near the campsite. He was fishing in the river now, skillfully catching fish.
“…Caught too many. I guess I’ll sell them.”
With that, Father put the fish he had caught in a basket and went to sell them to a merchant in the town. It seemed that the sales were better than he expected, and he was quite pleased.
“…Herbs too.”

He muttered under his breath, and though I could barely hear him, I remembered that around this time, Father had been making money from herbs. The grasslands had been thoroughly scouted, so it was understandable that resources were starting to dwindle. I followed him in secret, and that night, he camped out by the river. It seemed that he had become interested in the fishing equipment and was fiddling with it, or rather, he spent the whole night fishing. The next day. I made up an excuse to the crimson swine that we had grown stronger, and so we took the day off. The lazy crimson swine seemed happy to go to the spa. I made sure to quickly kick him out of the party so that he wouldn’t be able to find me.
“Hmm… well then—”

Father gathered his things, then sold the fish he had caught last night to the fishmonger, asking what would sell for the best price. The fishmonger seemed confused but appeared to explain what would sell well under the condition that the fish were fresh. When I asked the fishmonger later, it seemed Father had also asked about dried fish, likely looking to sell them if he had a surplus. It was becoming clear what Father was planning. Since herbs alone weren’t profitable, he was likely trying to earn money by fishing. I’m curious about how he plans to deal with the level issue, but it seems like he’s just trying to gather money for living expenses. I would gather money for him if I could, from anywhere. However, I must remain in the position of an enemy to him. I can’t afford to show him any favors. If he realizes I’m not his enemy, it might prevent Firo-tan from being born. Ah, monster merchant, please hurry up and make contact with Father. As I thought this, I followed Father as he gathered his things and began moving along the riverbank, avoiding the gaze of others.

Where is he going? I followed him as he moved, eventually arriving at a village. He paid for a ride on a shared carriage and headed to a coastal town. The town was a port city heading to Calmira Island. Afterwards, Father fished along the coast, changing fishing spots as he moved. It seemed like he had bought fishing bait and equipment for sea fishing, and he was skillfully catching fish. He would fill the basket with fish and continue on with a light step. The fish he caught were then sold cheaply to merchants in nearby villages or towns, similar to a fishmonger. Of course, he didn’t forget to gather herbs as well. Though he had to be cautious of monsters, Father was being careful as usual. In fact, any dangerous monsters approaching him had already been dealt with by me. So it went, as Father fished and made his way down the coastline.
Eventually… by the end of the day, Father arrived at the village he was supposed to develop, but it had become a deserted village.
“A deserted village? It feels a bit strange though…”

On high alert, Father began rummaging through the abandoned village where the older sister had lived. I already knew from previous loops that there wasn’t much valuable in the village, but Father seemed to be searching through the trash, looking for anything useful to put in his shield, perhaps hoping for a new one to appear. He then looked for a place to rest for the night, placing his belongings in a half-destroyed house before resuming his fishing. I silently watched Father. If he hadn’t bought the slave, he would have started fishing, moved from town to town, and eventually arrived at the village where the older sister had been. What a strange twist of fate. As night began to fall, Father cooked the fish he caught and had a meal. The fire he made in the empty village quietly lit the area, creating a sad, lonely atmosphere. I had to go back to the inn soon and nod along to the crimson swine’s pointless chatter. Just as I was thinking that…
“Waaooohhh—”

A distant howl echoed through the area. By the way, this area had been affected by the waves, and there should still be some remnants of the wave’s monsters here. There was also a strong sense that wild monsters were beginning to appear. Father, too, heightened his alertness and, holding his breath, increased the fire on his campfire. Soon, a group of monsters surrounded the village. It seemed like Father was preparing to escape if necessary, gathering his things in case of an emergency.

Would he… fight the monsters? As I prepared to launch a skill at the monsters trying to tighten their encirclement on him, a strong flash of light shot from the direction of the sea at the edge of the village. It pierced through the monsters.
“Ah? I thought someone had come back because I saw a fire in the village… but it seems I was wrong.”
And then, from the sea, the older sister’s older sister appeared and walked toward Father.
